units.brief: Battle Bus (GLA, T3, Arms Dealer plus Palace): cover the eight seats whose riders shoot out of it (passenger-sets-weapon, fire-port variant); its second life when the hull dies, a parked bunker with fresh health whose riders survive hurt and keep shooting until it falls; that getting out ends the bunker; the salvage armour step in notes; that it never ranks up; and the 1.03 change that stops Hijackers while anyone rides. Check which on_death term, if any, fits the bunker.

Combat Chinook (USA Air Force General, T1, Supply Center once a War Factory stands): cover the eight seats for infantry or vehicles; riders shooting from its ports (passenger-sets-weapon); the point-defence laser against missiles (an armour model, not a pattern); supply runs (gather-resources, not while it carries anyone); and Combat Drop, which ropes Rangers into a building (drop-in-from-above). Check on https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Combat_Chinook what the drop does to a building the enemy holds.

Technical (GLA, T1, Arms Dealer): cover the machine gun and the two salvage steps (a splash cannon, then a rocket launcher that point-defence lasers can stop), each recorded as an acquired weapon plus one triggered ability linking leech-weapon-on-kill, as the Generals notes say; that only GLA units see the crates and a dead GLA vehicle drops one too; its very high speed; and the open bed for five riders, who survive its death hurt. Juhziz's higher price goes in notes.

Overlord (China, T3, War Factory plus Propaganda Center): cover the twin cannons on the turret; running over enemy vehicles; and the single add-on bought in the field, one of three (a bunker for five shooters, a Gattling cannon that hits aircraft and infantry and spots stealth, a propaganda tower that heals it and nearby allies and speeds their fire), as upgrade-in-field, rally-allies, repair-allies and passenger-sets-weapon. Tao's faster, irradiating version and the generals who lack it go in notes.

Red Guard (China, T1, Barracks): cover the pair of riflemen trained together; the horde bonus (horde units fire faster while five or more stand together) as an innate passive with no pattern and a fit_note, as the Generals notes say; the Capture Building upgrade (capture-structure, source upgrade); and splash on the clump, such as flash-bangs, as the counter. Shin Fai's Mini-Gunner goes in notes.

Hacker (China, T3, Barracks plus Propaganda Center): cover the laptop that earns cash for his side while he stays set up, with income that rises as he ranks up from hacking (said in the ability summary, as the notes ask); the short-range hack that shuts an enemy building down while he keeps at it (capture-structure, sabotage variant); and that he is unarmed and fragile. Shin Fai's camouflaged Super Hacker goes in notes.

Aurora Bomber (USA, T3, Air Field plus Strategy Center): cover the supersonic run on which nothing can hit it; the one heavy bomb that cannot be jammed or shot down and does not follow a moving target; the slow, exposed trip home and the reload on a landing pad (jet, high air); and Granger's Fuel-Air and Alexander's Aurora Alpha versions in notes. Check whether become-invulnerable fits the run.

Sentry Drone (USA, T1, War Factory): cover the uncrewed body that crew snipes, Hijackers and neutron shells cannot touch (an immunity, with Jarmen Kell as a foiled enemy); camouflage while it stands still and holds fire (cloak); stealth detection around it (sensors); the optional gun bought in the field (upgrade-in-field); and that it never ranks up.

Drone Operator (GDF, T1, Barracks): cover his anti-tank pistol; the drone's small missiles at ground and air targets his side can already see; the toggle that roots him and hands him the drone on a leash; the toggle that sends it back to follow; the drone's replacement and its death with him; and the drone fighting on outside while he rides or garrisons (launch-drones, piloted variant). The Combat Drone page says the drones cannot be steered, which clashes with his toggle, and patch 2.0.0 made him a little faster.

Sentinel (GDF, T1, Vehicle Bay): cover the minigun that hits ground and air and, in multiplayer, marks its main target (weapon trait mark); the scanner-round toggle that marks every enemy around the one hit for little damage (switch-weapon-mode); what Marked does (more range and damage from GDF Networked weapons, Intel paid when the target dies); its very high speed and long sight; and its thin health. The page was last checked at 1.6.0, so read the patches since.

Shieldmaiden (GDF, T2, Satellite Uplink with Specialist Pod, built at the Vehicle Bay): cover the field that, while it stands still, slows every enemy rocket and missile weapon inside it to half rate (Missile Interference); the Intel-paid repair turret that mends allied vehicles nearby (deploy-turret, repair-allies); the long-range laser that hits only aircraft; hover rules (sets off no mines, neither crushes nor is crushed); and its Intel price at the registry's rate.

Line Officer (Dynasty, T2, Specialist Bureau): cover Inspire Troops (nearby infantry briefly move and fire faster: rally-allies); Supervise Crew (he boards a friendly vehicle, one officer each, which turns Elite while he rides, and he is thrown clear alive if it dies); what Elite gives per the Veterancy page; and his slow, heavy pistol. The page was checked at 1.4.0 and 2.0.0 gave the pistol more range, so read the patches between.

Voltaic Tank (Dynasty, T3, Defender upgrade, built at the Machine Shop): cover the beam that charges before each shot, jumps between packed vehicles and destroys any vehicle already in Tempest Overflow (execute-target); how allied weapons stack Tempest Charge up to Overflow; the short shutdown of defences it hits and its weak damage to buildings; and the Martial Plan trade of health for fire rate (overclock-self). https://tempestrising.wiki.gg/wiki/Tempest_Overflow leaves it out of the finisher list, so settle that conflict.

Tempest Sphere (Dynasty, T3, Defender upgrade, built at the Machine Shop): cover crushing everything smaller than itself (hover units and heavy vehicles escape); ramming bigger targets and the multiplayer Vulnerability that follows; the long-cooldown straight-line charge (dash); Tempest Plating, which turns Tempest Charge into repairs; the Demolitionist it leaves when destroyed; and its rolling ball body, for which the mobility and body lists have no term (record the gap).

Thunderhead (Veti, T2, Veti Eye with Initial Awakening, built at the Celestial Gate): cover that it is unarmed; the Lightning Rod it drops, a fortified pylon that soldiers and tanks walk into; the recall that dissolves the Rod and teleports everyone inside to the aircraft (build-linked-exits, teleport, carry-passengers); the Arcing zap at close attackers (that page gives two damage figures); its air layer; and the 2.0.0 rise in health and speed. Its page is unverified.

Vimana (Veti, T3, Veti Eye with Transcendent Awakening, built at the Celestial Gate, one per Gate): cover Gate Link (aircraft its Gate builds appear beside it: host-spawn-point); teleporting anywhere inside its owner's build area; the summoned Caretakers with Combat Servitors; the paid area Consecration (rally-allies); the Subjugation aura; the cannon that ignores resistances (Omni damage has no damage_map key); and its instant death when its Gate falls (depend-on-relay). The gate conflict and the unverified page need the 2.0.0 notes.

Enlightened (Veti, T1, appears free at the Resurrection Anchor; also from the Corral, Ambassador captures and Subjugated kills): cover its weak brawl attack; the key that sacrifices it to give allied units and buildings around it Consecration (less damage taken, more speed) plus a perk by receiver (reload, repair, a summoned Servitor, sight and detection, income) as rally-allies and resupply-allies; its use as fuel for Caretakers and Luminaries; the 2.0.0 changes; and that it is never bought (cost_band allows null only for games with no purchases, so record the gap).

Anna Kos and Wojtek (Polania, hero; take her gate and tier from the Iron Harvest notes, Headquarters or Reserve): cover her long rifle; the aimed shot that passes through every target on its line (fire-power-shot); the bear that brawls when sent, comes back when recalled and slowly heals nearby friendly soldiers, walking over to hurt ones (repair-allies); the bear as one lasting AI partner; and the knock-out and free revive of heroes from the notes.

Olga Morozova and Changa (Rusviet, hero; gate and tier from the notes; her page is titled Olga Romanova): cover stealth that holds until an enemy comes near or she acts and returns once none is close (cloak); remote charges stuck on mechs or buildings that go off when she walks out of range (throw-explosive); calling and riding the tiger for speed, visible while mounted (transform); the tiger fighting briefly when an attack drops her off; and her price from the DevBlogs.

PZM-13 'Mocny' (Polania, T2, Advanced Workshop): cover its two modes, walking (direct cannon fire and smoke that keeps surrounding it as it moves) and planted (a longer, harder cannon and a smoke shell that leaves a fixed screen where it lands), as deploy-siege-mode and lay-smoke; the DevBlog #45 price; its rear damage, where its page and Changelog #06 disagree (follow the notes); and its in-game name.

Sd. KS 49 'Grimbart' (Saxony, T1, Saxon Workshop): cover the gatling; the key sweep that roots it and fires across an arc the player sizes, a wider arc holding it in place longer (suppress-with-fire); DevBlog #35's change that made its normal gun suppress too and the sweep pin harder; its Reserve II listing; and anti-mech guns as its counter.

William Mason (Usonia, hero; gate and tier from the notes): cover the exosuit's burst cannon; climbing out and leaving the suit as a fixed turret while he runs with a revolver (deploy-turret); ordering the empty suit to rocket-jump back to him (transform); the automatic eject before the suit is wrecked (on_death pilot-eject); calling a new suit to crash down at a spot he picks after a cooldown (drop-in-from-above); the suit's armour per the notes; and his class (power-suit infantry or walker).

M-22 'Stark' (Usonia, T2, Usonian Advanced Workshop): cover the pneumatic jackhammer for mechs and the side flamethrower for infantry, both used on the move; Berserk (more damage the more hurt it is); the key that shuts it down for a few seconds to patch itself, helpless meanwhile (heal-self); and Lech Kos's matching rage in notes.

SHM-68 'Nakovalnya' (Rusviet, T1, Rusviet Workshop): cover the rocket barrage aimed by hand at an area with no set-up (bombard-area); Sentry Mode, a veteran ability that anchors it and fires single rockets by itself at anything entering a small chosen zone (deploy-siege-mode, zone-anchor variant, source veterancy); its class by how it moves (two big wheels pushed by small legs, though the game calls it a mech); rear damage per the notes; and its weakness up close.

Engineer squad (shared, T1, any faction's Headquarters, Barracks or Advanced Barracks): cover sandbags and barbed wire (build-cover); anti-armour mines (lay-mines); repairing mechs and buildings (repair-allies); building base structures; its weak gun; and its place as the stock crew of weapon systems. Record it once under shared, as the weapon systems are, name each faction's version in notes, and flag that the shared faction's registry note names only aircraft and weapon systems.
